newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends softer despite Colombian news. [CORRECTED 16:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends softer despite Colombian news. [CORRECTED 16:42 GMT]

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended a quiet session softer on Monday, with the market unperturbed by reports of a sharp drop in Colombian coffee exports.
Traders said Colombian coffee, if scarce, could be substituted by Central American beans.
"The Mexican crop is about ready for export and the market is now awaiting estimates for Brazil's 1997/98 crop," said one trader. (Corrects Brazilian crop year from 1996/97)
"The Brazilian 97/98 crop looks like it will be a good one," he adding, noting that flowering is beginning to take place.
At the close on Monday the benchmark November contract was off $2 at $1,480 but above a session low of $1,475 a tonne.
Turnover on the exchange reached 3,904 lots.

And despite some light pre-winter coverage, traders said the market was not stirred by reports that Colombian January-August coffee exports were down 12.8 percent at 6.57 million 60-kg bags after unusually heavy rains earlier this year.
"The market is wary of what is coming out from origin," said another trader.
